notes: The court, its gate and the beggar's corner are Scene 7's shared place; the rented room and the famine market are drawn here, each on its own grid.

The last feast is one stitched take, W01 to W06, a baton pass that follows the coin from Asher's purse to the wine-seller, past Kallias's stroke to Jes leaving at the gate, then whips back to find Asher.
Scenes 1A and 6B flash the purse tipped over the wine-seller's open palm and the single coin falling, from W01 at about 11.5 to 13.5 s, close at knee height.
Kallias now sits at the west table and Philon on the north-west couch, so the life of the feast has moved to the gate end and Asher drinks alone at the head couch under the lamps he paid for.
Philon's new friend in the court is an unnamed guest; the new boy first appears at the gate, where the screenplay introduces him.

The rented room opens south onto a lodging-house yard, so the noon light through the shutter falls across his face and the landlord stands dark in the door against the white yard, the jenny tethered beyond him.
The famine market runs east to west, so the hot east wind drives the grit down its length toward the opening wide; Asher walks up the street into it and leaves barefoot with it at his back.

The market is one take, W11 to W16; the camera goes down to knee height with each thing he gives up, the cloak, the sandals, the belt with the empty purse, and follows the merchant's eyes to the sling.

At the gate the camera stays low against the wall beside Asher for one take, W17 to W21, turning once up the street with his look and back; in W20, the scene's one chosen stillness, the company's lamps slide across the sleeve over his face and away through the gate, the design note's signature move.
The shared place draws the gate leaf open; it stands open with the beggar's corner in the post's shadow until the company is in, then the house servant shuts it and the dark comes back.
